# Base image with Flux, OpenMPI, and AWS EFA support for ARM
FROM ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Set versions for OSU Benchmarks
ENV OSU_BENCHMARKS_VERSION=7.3

# Install build dependencies, download, compile, and install OSU benchmarks
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    autoconf \
    automake \
    libtool && \
    # Create a temporary directory for the build
    mkdir -p /tmp/build && \
    cd /tmp/build && \
    # Download the OSU benchmarks source code
    wget "https://mvapich.cse.ohio-state.edu/download/mvapich/osu-micro-benchmarks-${OSU_BENCHMARKS_VERSION}.tar.gz" && \
    tar -xvf "osu-micro-benchmarks-${OSU_BENCHMARKS_VERSION}.tar.gz" && \
    cd "osu-micro-benchmarks-${OSU_BENCHMARKS_VERSION}" && \
    # Configure the build to use the MPI compilers from the base image
    ./configure CC=mpicc CXX=mpicxx && \
    # Build the benchmarks
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # FIX: Corrected path to find compiled MPI executables from 'mpi' to 'c/mpi'
    find c/mpi -type f -executable -exec cp {} /usr/local/bin/ \; && \
    # Clean up build artifacts and package manager cache
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /tmp/build && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set a default command to show that a key executable is available
CMD ["osu_latency", "--help"]

flux-minicluster-manifest.item:
# MiniCluster manifest for running the OSU Latency benchmark on AWS ARM CPU instances.
# This configuration is designed for a 2-node job utilizing EFA for networking.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the MiniCluster job.
  name: flux-osu-latency-aws
  # The job will be deployed to the 'default' Kubernetes namespace.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Specifies the number of pods in the MiniCluster job. Set to 2 to run across two nodes.
  size: 2
  # Total number of MPI tasks. The OSU latency benchmark is a point-to-point test requiring 2 processes.
  tasks: 2

  # Keep pods and associated resources after the job completes for inspection and debugging.
  cleanup: false

  # Enable strict logging for better diagnostics.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Flux Operator specific settings.
  flux:
    # Specify the target architecture is ARM, as required for AWS Graviton or similar instances.
    arch: "arm"
    # NOTE: The following container spec is provided to satisfy instructions,
    # but it will be IGNORED by the operator because 'disable' is set to true below.
    # This configuration assumes Flux is pre-installed in the main application container.
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy
      # Disabling the injected flux sidecar container as per instructions.
      disable: true

  # Defines the application container. Only one container is specified.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:osu-latency
      # The command to execute. The Flux Operator will prepend `flux run -n <tasks>`.
      command: osu_latency
      # This container is a worker, not the one launching the job. This MUST be false.
      launcher: false
      # Always pull the latest image to ensure the most recent version is used for experiments.
      imagePullPolicy: Always
      # Requesting AWS EFA resources for high-performance, low-latency networking.
      # The value is a string "1" as is standard for device plugin resources.
      resources:
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"

manager.name: Build and Deploy OSU Latency
manager.description: Build a Docker container and deploy it as a Kubernetes Job.

context.environment: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes to run across nodes
context.details:
You MUST use ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm as a base image. It includes OpenMPI and libfabric provided from the efa installer for AWS and the entire Flux Framework stack.
You MUST compile setting the cxx compiler to mpicxx and the c compiler to mpicc.
Build the OSU benchmarks. You MUST have MPI support enabled. You MUST ensure osu_latency is on the path.
You MUST build for a multi-node MPI environment

context.resources: The resource spec you got earlier is for an autoscaling cluster, so the nodes possible are not there. You must add the nodeSelector to use node.kubernetes.io/instance-type m7g.16xlarge with 64 CPU, 256 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton3).
context.details:
Run The OSU Latency benchmark across 2 nodes.
You MUST run on 2 nodes and you MUST set flux.container.disable to true.
You MUST set the containers imagePullPolicy to Always.
The Flux Operator uses flux run in the pwd with the tasks determined by the spec.tasks.
You MUST set resource requests and limits to use vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
Since this is an ARM instance you MUST change the flux.container.image to be
ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy and set flux.arch: "arm".
